topic: the 1917 French army mutiny after Nivelle's failed 48-hour victory promise
title: He Promised To Win WWI In 48 Hours. His Army Mutinied Instead.
description: In 1917, French General Robert Nivelle promised to end World War One in 48 hours. When his offensive collapsed, nearly half of France's army refused to keep attacking, though they stayed in their trenches to defend. Original AI-narrated historical commentary, written from public historical sources, not a repost of any single video.

hook_candidates.text: In 1917, half the French army mutinied, but they never actually stopped fighting.
In 1917, a French general promised to win the war in 48 hours.
What happens when half an army refuses to fight, but keeps holding the line?
In 1917, General Robert Nivelle bet his career on one 48-hour promise.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists a secret that big could never stay hidden, because they want to prove one nearly did, for decades.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume that when an army mutinies, it stops fighting entirely, but half of this French army mutinied in 1917 and never actually stopped fighting, they only refused to attack.
closing_comment: The wildest part is Nivelle's 48-hour promise turned into weeks of failed attacks before this French army mutiny even started. Ever notice how the boldest promises are usually the first ones to fall apart?

sources.note: Confirms Nivelle promised victory in 48 hours with 10,000 expected casualties; offensive ran weeks beyond that target.
Confirms 54 divisions, about half the French Army, mutinied by June 1917, refusing to attack but still defending trenches.
Confirms German intelligence received reports of the unrest but didn't act on them, missing the war's biggest opportunity.
